first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and two inherited findings indicate that reducing signup friction and shortening onboarding improved durable activation, completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. This aligns more directly with sustainable qualified revenue than promotional pricing, which carries a documented 30-day retention penalty. Verify both onboarding records to confirm segment applicability, implementation details, and downstream revenue or retention effects before launch.

final.rationale: Run a targeted onboarding-simplification experiment only for simple SMB accounts, explicitly excluding complex-workspace accounts. The evidence directly addresses the current completion and activation declines: signup simplification increased activation 9% and qualified revenue 4%, while shortened onboarding increased completion 13% and reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days. Keep the test guarded because signup simplification showed a small 30-day retention decline and shortened onboarding increased 60-day churn 9% in complex workspaces. Measure qualified revenue with 30- and 60-day retention/churn guardrails before considering expansion; do not generalize beyond the verified segment.
